### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

When serving a hybrid Mamba model with hierarchical cache enabled, the SGLang scheduler's event loop intermittently blocks for over 3 minutes, making the server unresponsive to `/health` checks and all incoming requests. This leads to process termination (SIGKILL) by the container runtime.

1. **Silent event loop hang**: The server stops responding with no error in logs. The last logged request completes normally, then no further log output appears. Metrics scrape returns empty until the process is killed and restarted.

2. **Long TTFT stall before hang**: A single request exhibits **222-second TTFT** (`e2e_latency: 225s`), during which the scheduler is blocked and cannot process `/health` or any other request. After this request completes, the server receives SIGTERM and shuts down.

In both cases:
- No OOM, no CUDA error, no `AssertionError`, no NaN in logs
- `mamba_available_tokens = 0` with `mamba_evictable_tokens ≈ 68` (free-list empty but evictable slots exist)

### Reproduction

The issue is intermittent and requires production-scale traffic to reproduce. However, the conditions that trigger it are:

1. Hybrid Mamba model with hierarchical cache enabled
2. `mamba_available_tokens` drops to 0 (free-list exhausted)
3. `mamba_evictable_tokens > 0` (eviction is attempted)
4. A large-context request arrives (e.g., 100K+ tokens)
5. Scheduler blocks on eviction I/O → `/health` timeout → process kill

### Environment

- **SGLang version**: v0.5.14
- **Model**: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 (hybrid Mamba), TP=8
- **Hardware**: H100 80GB × 8 per replica
- **Launch command**:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model /mnt/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 \
    --tp 8 \
    --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
    --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
    --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
    --speculative-num-steps 3 \
    --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
    --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
    --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer \
    --flashinfer-allreduce-fusion-backend=auto \
    --mem-fraction-static 0.79 \
    --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load": true, "num_threads": 64}' \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8088 \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --enable-metrics \
    --enable-cache-report \
    --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 32 \
    --mamba-full-memory-ratio 0.3 \
    --enable-hierarchical-cache \
    --hicache-ratio 16 \
    --hicache-write-policy write_through_selective \
    --hicache-io-backend direct \
    --hicache-mem-layout page_first_direct \
    --max-running-request 32 \
    --page-size 64
```

comments.body: @HyeonjeCho Is the issue still there? How long it will take to trigger the hanging? Could you try `write_through` policy?

Second independent report of what looks like the same family, without HiCache.

Setup: single DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121, 128 GB unified), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 (hybrid GDN + QSA, 36/48 linear layers), day-0 image `lmsysorg/sglang:qwen38flashnext` (0.0.0.dev1+gd91c3682b) plus two local patches (PLE table mmap, sm_121 QSA decode kernel from #36845), `--speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer --mem-fraction-static 0.79 --chunked-prefill-size 1024`, max_total_num_tokens 159,552. No hierarchical cache.

Two hangs in one day, same signature: frontend alive (`/health` 200, `/get_load` reports 0 requests), every new completion hangs, scheduler process in R state at 100 % CPU, GPU at idle power. Nothing in the log after the last batch line.

1. `--max-running-requests 2`: one ~109k-token conversation decoding at `full token usage: 0.98, mamba usage: 0.50` (mamba num 4), a second ~109k request admitted at 03:03:10, never scheduled. Stuck 9 hours until killed.
2. `--max-running-requests 1`: four ~80k prompts served sequentially (all cached by RadixAttention), then a ~93k prompt: prefill completes (`#pending-token: 0, full token usage: 0.89, #cached-token: 0, mamba usage: 0.57`) at 13:15:27 and no decode batch ever follows. Killed after 6 minutes by an external health probe (a 2-token generation) that distinguishes this from a healthy server, since `/health` keeps answering.

3. Same day, after `/flush_cache` returned "Cache flushed successfully": a single ~120k-token prompt is queued (`#queue-req: 1, #running-req: 0`) and never admitted; no prefill line for it in 5 minutes, scheduler at 100 % CPU, killed by the same external probe.

The boot log reports `Mamba Cache is allocated. max_mamba_cache_size: 9 ... max_running_requests is capped to 1 by the mamba state cache (max_mamba_cache_size=9, 5 state slots per request)`, and `mamba usage` sits at 0.50-0.57 right before each hang, so the mamba state pool (rather than the KV token pool) looks like the resource that runs out; with chunked prefill at 1024 a 120k prompt also creates ~117 interior checkpoints (#36935) against 9 slots. Controlled reproduction, same box, same day, one prompt at a time with `/flush_cache` before each: with the default cache of 9 slots (5 per running request) the second ~100-120k prompt never leaves the queue (4 of 4 attempts on such boots); with 15 slots, six consecutive 60k prompts and two 120k prompts all served. The default size itself varied between 9 and 15 from one boot to the next on identical flags (memory left after weights). Setting `--max-mamba-cache-size` explicitly is not a workaround here: the explicit branch reserves far more memory (K=9 explicit: max_total_num_tokens 104k instead of 159k; K=24: 59k), and the automatic size did not respond the way I expected to the other knobs on this build (same box, same day, `--mem-fraction-static 0.79`): auto with `--max-running-requests 1` gave 9 or 15 slots on different boots (KV pool 159,552 both times); `--mamba-full-memory-ratio 1.2` kept 9 slots and shrank the pool to 89,600; `--max-running-requests 2` gave 8 slots and 112,384; explicit 9 gave 104,128, explicit 15 gave 94,592, explicit 24 gave 59,136. A request longer than the pool (60k on the 59k pool) also spins instead of being refused.

The discriminating experiment: `SGLANG_OPT_MAMBA_SKIP_DECODE_LOCK=1` (state cache 8 slots, 4 per request) served four consecutive 60k prompts, the third and fourth of which needed an eviction, on the same box where the default locking (9 slots, 5 per request) hung on the second prompt every time. So the cached state locked during decode is what the scheduler can never evict, and it keeps trying forever instead of failing the request.

Native stack of the spinning thread (gdb, 4th occurrence, 99.9 % of one core, `/proc/<pid>/syscall` = running, wchan 0): `zmq_msg_recv` -> `poll` under `_PyEval_EvalFrameDefault`, i.e. the scheduler event loop itself busy-polling with one request queued and never admitted. py-spy cannot read this process while it spins (EFAULT), so the Python-level frame is still missing; the loop never logs. Happy to test a candidate fix or an env flag that makes the admission failure visible.

Author of #36935 here. This looks like the same core resource failure in two different lock states.

In both setups, the mamba pool can't supply the slots the next request needs. Mine had evictable interior checkpoints under LRU, so it degraded silently (hits dropped to 0 tokens, but completed). Yours had the remainder in states locked during decode that apparently never get released — so eviction couldn't progress and got stuck in an infinite retry loop, even with nothing running (your post-flush case). That aligns directly with your SKIP_DECODE_LOCK=1 finding. At the default 9-slot boots, there's no margin left between normal operation and a total lockup.

For a unified fix: when admission/eviction stalls on locked slots, we should fail the request or issue a warning instead of infinite retrying. Combined with the startup warning in #36935, this would give us solid visibility into these failures.

title: [Bug] Scheduler event loop blocks on Mamba eviction under large-context requests, causing server hang and process kill
